---
title: "Choose the physical problem"
description: "Capacitance, resonant modes or a driven response: what each calculation asks, what it returns and which solver runs it, with numbers from the SimplePad."
scgsim-kind: "concept"
scgsim-status: "CONVERGING"
scgsim-id: "docs/concepts/problems"
---

From one layout SCGSim can compute three kinds of answer: a capacitance
matrix, the resonant modes, or the response to a signal at a port. Choose the
one whose output is the circuit quantity you need. The capacitance and mode
examples are the [First simulation](../start/first-simulation.qmd) pad: a
200 µm square pad in a 20 µm gap inside ground metal, on a 1000 µm chip. The
driven example is a through line: two launchers joined by 900 µm of
coplanar waveguide.

| Problem | It asks | It returns | Solvers | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Capacitance | How much charge each conductor holds per volt | A capacitance matrix, in farads | Palace Electrostatic, Q3D | 112.54 fF between the pad and the ground ([First simulation](../start/first-simulation.qmd); one solve on the first mesh) |
| Resonant modes | At which frequencies the layout rings, and where the energy sits | Frequency and $Q$ of each mode; on request, energy participation | Palace Eigenmode, HFSS Eigenmode | Mode 1 at 5.135702 GHz with a 10 nH junction across the gap ([recorded Palace run](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/issues/84#issuecomment-6789403273); at most two refinement passes) |
| Driven response | How the layout responds to a signal at its ports, frequency by frequency | Complex S-parameters versus frequency, with a Touchstone file | Palace Driven, HFSS Driven Terminal | \|S21\| above −0.006 dB and \|S11\| below −29.8 dB from 2 to 10 GHz ([S-parameters with Palace](../guides/s-parameters-palace.qmd); second-order elements) |

A fourth calculation, Q2D, gives per-unit-length properties of a line's
cross-section; [below](#finite-extraction-versus-a-cross-section).

## Capacitance {#capacitance-charge-response-to-conductor-voltage}

A capacitance calculation sets each **terminal**, a conductor you name, to 1 V
in turn, holds the ground at 0 V and computes the charge on every conductor.
The result is the capacitance matrix, in the order of the terminals; how to
read its diagonal and off-diagonal entries is on the
[First simulation](../start/first-simulation.qmd#read-the-result) page. What
you ground is part of the problem: a box whose walls are grounded is a
different model from one where only the chip's ground metal is at 0 V.

## Resonant modes {#resonance-modes-of-a-field-and-circuit-model}

An Eigenmode calculation finds the frequencies at which the model resonates
and the field of each mode. A Josephson junction enters as a linear
inductance on a port sheet across its gap, 10 nH in the example; the drawn
pad alone has no such element. For an ideal lumped circuit,
$f_0=1/(2\pi\sqrt{LC})$ is a useful reference, but the field calculation
includes the distributed fields and the box around the chip.

Palace and HFSS run Eigenmode. On request they also compute energy
participation: where the mode's energy sits and what given loss assumptions
imply for its $Q$; read [Energy participation and Surface EPR](surface-epr.qmd)
before using those numbers.

## Driven response {#driven-response-excite-a-port-at-a-frequency}

A driven calculation applies a signal at a port and computes the response at
each frequency of a sweep. Palace Driven and HFSS Driven Terminal do this with
lumped ports on port sheets of the layout and return the S-parameters. A peak
in a driven response and an Eigenmode frequency are two different results; one
does not replace the other. Which ports each solver takes is on
[Supported calculations](../reference/supported-calculations.qmd).

## Cross-section {#finite-extraction-versus-a-cross-section}

Q3D extracts the matrix of a finite 3D model. Q2D extracts per-unit-length
capacitance, conductance, inductance and resistance of a cross-section you
declare, for a line that is uniform along its length. Neither replaces the
other: a per-unit-length matrix carries nothing about a finite length, its ends
or its ports.

::: {.callout-tip title="Choose a quantity before a solver"}
Write down the conductor pair, mode or port response you need, its units and
how your circuit model will use it. Then choose a workflow from
[Supported calculations](../reference/supported-calculations.qmd).
:::

For the solvers' own formulations, see
[Palace problem types](https://awslabs.github.io/palace/stable/guide/problem/)
and the [PyAEDT user guide](https://aedt.docs.pyansys.com/version/stable/User_guide/index.html).
